name: PAD Amputation Index Level and Guillotine Sequence (pad_amp v2, base-module sub-graph)
remarks: WHAT THIS IS, AND HOW TO INSTALL IT
The INDEX-EVENT sub-graph for pad_amp v2: incident amputation level, the
guillotine/definitive split, and the guillotine closure sequence that CLASSIFIES
the incident level. Destined for pad_amp_base.json once module composition is
wired (synthetic_data/registry.yaml :: pad_amp).
⛔ IT IS A DROP-IN REPLACEMENT, NOT AN ADDITIONAL MODULE. Exactly one module
may own the index procedure — two owners is what inflated the v1 cohort ~2x (the
379 -> 196 correction). Install by REPLACING three states in pad_amp_dispo.json:
DELETE  Index_Procedure_Branch   (Simple, 0.4 AKA / 0.6 BKA)
DELETE  Index_Procedure_AKA      (Procedure, SNOMED 79733001)
DELETE  Index_Procedure          (Procedure, SNOMED 88312006)
IN-EDGE   Index_Admission_Encounter -> Index_Level_Draw
OUT-EDGE  every terminal state here -> Post_Index_Inpatient_Delay
The in- and out-edges are unchanged, so dispo's discharge-disposition, ED and
readmission logic downstream is untouched. The closure procedures deliberately
fire BEFORE the out-edge, i.e. while the index admission encounter is still
open — a staged amputation is one longer admission, which is also why guillotine
patients should show a longer LOS.
WHY THIS EXISTS: THE CLOSURE DEFINES THE INDEX LEVEL
MoRe, Methods, 'Defining incident amputation level', verbatim:
'For guillotine procedures at the TT and TF level, it was assumed that a
closure procedure would be performed within three weeks; therefore, a search
forward three weeks for the next procedure code was performed TO CLASSIFY THE
INCIDENT LEVEL. If the next subsequent procedure was more than three weeks
after the initial guillotine procedure or there was no subsequent procedure,
an error in the initial coding was presumed and the guillotine code was
recoded as a definitive amputation.'
So the closure is not an event that FOLLOWS the index — it DETERMINES it. A
guillotine TT closed at TF is an incident TF. That is why this belongs to the
index-owning module and not to pad_amp_reamp.json, which consumes
amp_index_level and amp_index_definitive as INPUTS.
⭐ GUILLOTINES OCCUR ONLY AT TT AND TF. MoRe says so explicitly ('at the TT and
TF level'). TM is always definitive. This has a consequence that was previously
got wrong: the overall guillotine share is 20% of TT/TF patients = 13.2% of ALL
index patients, NOT 20% of all. An earlier pad_amp_reamp simulation assumed 20%
of everyone.
THE INITIAL LEVEL DRAW IS CORRECTED, AND MUST BE
Escalation at closure migrates patients from TT to TF, so drawing the published
mix directly would leave the FINAL mix wrong. Solved 2026-08-06:
leak = P(guillotine|TT) x P(closure within 3wk) x P(escalate) = 0.20 x 0.85 x 0.125 = 0.02125
INITIAL draw (this module)     FINAL mix (what the cohort sees)   published
⚠️ RE-SOLVE THE INITIAL DRAW if P(guillotine) or P(escalate) is retuned. The
arithmetic is t_TT = 43.7% / (1 - leak) and t_TF = 22.5% - t_TT x leak, where leak includes P(closure within 3wk).
THE THREE CLOSURE BRANCHES — all required, and branch (b) is the sharp one
Registry acceptance criterion 2 requires all three. An earlier draft implemented
only (a).
(a) CLOSURE WITHIN 3 WEEKS — days 1-21, ~85% of guillotines
Emits a SECOND DEFINITIVE AMPUTATION CODE. That code sets the level:
~87.5% same level, ~12.5% escalated TT->TF.
amp_index_definitive = false  -> pad_amp_reamp uses the 22-365 window
amp_decoy_early_revision = true
⭐ THIS IS THE STRONGEST NEGATIVE CONTROL IN THE DATASET. It is a second
amputation code at the same level, 1-2 weeks out, that is PART OF THE
INDEX EVENT and must NOT count as a re-amputation. Nothing distinguishes
it from a real re-amputation except the date — which is exactly why a
stump-revision code (the earlier mistake) was a far weaker test.
(b) CLOSURE AFTER 3 WEEKS — days 22-42, ~10% of guillotines
MoRe recodes the guillotine as definitive, so the index level is the
GUILLOTINE's level and amp_index_definitive = true. The late closure then
falls INSIDE the 1-365 definitive window, so it IS a re-amputation.
⭐ THE SAME CODE AT DAY 20 vs DAY 25 FLIPS FROM INDEX-EVENT TO OUTCOME.
That pair is the sharpest available test of the two-window rule, and no
other construct in the dataset tests it.
⚠️ This module therefore sets amp_reamp_occurred = true, so pad_amp_reamp
does not double-count. See the calibration note below.
(c) NO CLOSURE — ~5% of guillotines
Same recoding as (b): level = the guillotine's, definitive = true.
MoRe states BOTH this and the >3-week branch; ref 10 states only the
>3-week one, so an implementation following ref 10 misses this entirely.
The 85 / 10 / 5 split is RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS — MoRe implies (a) is the norm ('it
was assumed that a closure procedure would be performed within three weeks') and
treats (b) and (c) as coding errors, but publishes no frequencies.
⚠️ CALIBRATION INTERACTION WITH pad_amp_reamp.json — MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED
Branch (b) hands ~1.32% of ALL index patients a re-amputation before
pad_amp_reamp runs (13.2% guillotine x 10% late closure). Those patients enter
the monthly loop with amp_reamp_occurred already true, so they skip the
re-amputation hazard and go straight to the ELEVATED death hazard.
⭐ AN EARLIER NOTE HERE PREDICTED THIS WOULD PUSH THE MARGINAL FROM 27.7% TO
~29.0% AND THAT THE HAZARDS WOULD NEED RE-SOLVING. THAT WAS WRONG — it counted
the addition and ignored an offsetting effect built into the same design:
+ branch (b) adds re-amputations, but only ~1.32% x (1 - 0.277) = ~0.95% net,
since those patients would mostly have had one from the hazards anyway;
- branch (a) sets amp_index_definitive = false for ~11.3% of patients, which
triggers pad_amp_reamp's day-22 suppression and removes ONE of their twelve
monthly hazard draws.
The two nearly cancel. A composed simulation (300,000 patients, both modules
walked end to end, 2026-08-06) re-solved the hazard scales to 1.00 / 1.00 — i.e.
NO ADJUSTMENT NEEDED. Composed result:
total absolute error 0.37 pp
marginals: re-amputation 27.81% (28.0), death 19.53% (19.4)
Keep pad_amp_reamp's hazards at 0.0288 / 0.0403 / 0.0173 and 0.0156 / 0.0289.
RE-SIMULATE THE COMPOSED SYSTEM, not either module alone, after any retune —
that is the whole lesson of this note.
⛔ TODO [VOCAB] THE GUILLOTINE CODES ARE CPT4-ONLY. THIS IS THE BLOCKER.
Verified against local omop_vocab 2026-08-06: there is NO SNOMED
guillotine-amputation concept. Every SNOMED 'guillotine' hit is unrelated
(tonsillectomy, paper cutter, execution). The only options are CPT4:
27882  Amputation, leg, through tibia and fibula; open, circular
(guillotine)                                  -> OMOP 2105448  standard
27592  Amputation, thigh, through femur, any level; open, circular
(guillotine)                                  -> OMOP 2105211  standard
This module emits CPT4 for those two states. pad_amp_dispo.json has only ever
emitted SNOMED-CT / RxNorm / LOINC, so CPT4 is UNPROVEN through this ETL.
BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GUILLOTINE OUTPUT, run Steps 4-5 and confirm:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM procedure_occurrence WHERE procedure_concept_id IN (2105448, 2105211);
If that returns 0, the ETL is dropping CPT4 and:
* the day-22 window is untestable,
* branch (b)'s day-20-vs-day-25 flip cannot be constructed,
* registry acceptance criterion 2 cannot be met.
The fix is to extend the ETL's vocabulary handling. Do NOT substitute a
definitive SNOMED code for the guillotine — that silently converts every
guillotine patient into a definitive one and produces a PASSING pre-flight that
tests nothing.
OUTPUT ATTRIBUTES (consumed by pad_amp_reamp.json)
amp_index_level            'TM' | 'TT' | 'TF'  — final, post-closure
amp_index_definitive       true | false        — false only for branch (a)
amp_decoy_early_revision   true                — branch (a) only
amp_reamp_occurred         true                — branch (b) only
amp_reamp_subtype          'same_level'        — branch (b) only
amp_index_guillotine       true | false        — QC handle
amp_index_closure_branch   'within_3wk' | 'late' | 'none' | NA

⚠️ THESE ARE THE CORRECTED INITIAL SHARES, NOT THE PUBLISHED MIX.
Escalation at closure migrates TT -> TF, so drawing 33.8/43.7/22.5 here
would leave the FINAL mix wrong. See the header for the arithmetic.
Re-solve if P(guillotine) or P(escalate) changes.

remarks: The three branches MoRe requires. 85/10/5 is RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS — MoRe
implies (a) is the norm and treats (b)/(c) as coding errors, but publishes
no frequencies.
Days 1-21 — inside MoRe's three-week search by construction. Day 21 is the
boundary that must NOT count as a re-amputation, against day 22 which must.
This is the 1-2 week second-BKA-code pattern seen in real claims.
The closure CLASSIFIES the level. ~12.5% are closed higher than the
guillotine (TT -> TF) — a guillotine implies marginal tissue viability.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS, and the Index_Level_Draw shares above must be re-solved
if this changes.
⭐ THE STRONGEST NEGATIVE CONTROL. A SECOND definitive TT code 1-21 days
after the guillotine — identical to the index code, distinguished ONLY by
date. Part of the INDEX EVENT; must NOT count as a re-amputation.

codes.display: Amputation of leg through tibia and fibula [vocab query — OMOP 4338257]

remarks: ESCALATED at closure — guillotine was TT, closure is TF, so per MoRe the
INCIDENT LEVEL IS TF. A SQL that takes the level from the guillotine code
rather than the closure will mis-level exactly these patients.
Same three branches. No escalation arm — TF has nowhere higher within MoRe's levels.
Second definitive TF code, days 1-21. Negative control, as Closure_Procedure_TT.
definitive = FALSE. This is what makes pad_amp_reamp apply MoRe's 22-365
day window to these patients instead of 1-365.
Ground truth: the closure must NOT be counted as a re-amputation. QC asserts an exact count.
Branch (b), days 22-42. MoRe: 'an error in the initial coding was presumed
and the guillotine code was recoded as a definitive amputation.'
⭐ THE SHARPEST TEST IN THE DATASET: the SAME code at day 20 is part of the
index event, at day 25 it is an outcome. Nothing else tests that.

remarks: Level comes from the GUILLOTINE, not the late closure — the guillotine was recoded as the definitive index.
Guillotine recoded as definitive -> the 1-365 day window applies, so the late closure IS eligible.
⚠️ CALIBRATION INTERACTION. The late closure sits inside the 1-365 window, so
it IS a re-amputation. Flagging it here stops pad_amp_reamp double-counting
— its Reamp_Already_Occurred_Check skips these patients to the ELEVATED death
hazard. Costs ~1.32% of all patients as 'free' re-amputations, pushing the
marginal from ~27.7% to ~29.0%, so pad_amp_reamp's monthly hazards MUST be
re-solved once this module is installed.
Branch (c). No closure ever appears, so the guillotine is recoded as the
definitive index at its own level — which the provisional Set_Level_*_Initial
already holds, so only definitive needs setting.
MoRe states this branch; ref 10 states only the >3-week one, so an
implementation following ref 10 misses it entirely.
⛔ ON INSTALL, REPOINT THIS AT Post_Index_Inpatient_Delay in
pad_amp_dispo.json. It is a Terminal only so this file validates standalone.
